family.tagline: Four rooms of their own, one Companion Core, and a fountain out front.
family.story: Eszter runs the household from the Salon, and Gabor builds a weather station in the Games Den. Bence, sixteen, has the TV Room, and Reka, thirteen, studies in the West Bedroom. One Companion Core on the Salon shelf serves all four.

companion.name: Basil
companion.job: Drafts Eszter’s letters and replies from the notes she messages it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Eszter reads and sends every reply.

companion.name: Sorrel
companion.job: Drafts Gabor’s notes to suppliers from the part names he sends it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Gabor reads and sends every note.

popup.title: The parcel reaches the top step
popup.body: A Companion Core waits on the top step, under the geranium window boxes. Bence and Reka carry it through the stair hall to the Salon.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Reka reads the guide aloud while Gabor lifts the Core out.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Gabor plugs the Core in, and Bence presses the button. It wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: Standing by the shelf, Eszter opens the Wi-Fi settings on her phone and joins the Core’s own network. Then she chooses the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agent and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Eszter picks Hermes, and the family adds Yuvomi and LibreOffice. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Basil says hello
popup.body: Eszter types a first message to Basil, the agent she named. Basil answers from the Core.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: eszter
say.text: Hello, Eszter. This is Basil. What shall we do first?

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Eszter finds the pump invoice
popup.body: The pool pump coughs on a warm Tuesday, and the installer’s invoice is somewhere in last year’s paper. One word typed into Paperless-ngx on the Core finds the tagged scan.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains at the DNS level for devices that use it

popup.title: Gabor stops the banner ads
popup.body: Gabor’s tablet loads a weather forum with fewer banner ads. The router now sends lookups to Pi-hole on the Core, which drops ad and tracker domains for devices using it.

beats.capability: the LibreOffice suite (Writer, Calc and more) in your browser

popup.title: Eszter writes up the half-term plan
popup.body: Half-term needs a plan, so Eszter writes it in LibreOffice. It runs on the Core, shows in her browser and saves there.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Basil drafts the stonemason’s reply
popup.body: Eszter asks Basil to answer the stonemason’s quote. Basil drafts it on the Core’s local model, using dates she connected to Companion Memory. Eszter reads and sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: eszter
say.text: Here is the draft reply to the stonemason. Please read it, then send it.

beats.capability: host your own git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: A breeze fools the rain gauge
popup.body: A breeze fools the rooftop rain gauge, so Gabor opens an issue and merges the fix in Forgejo. The code and issues stay on the Core.

beats.capability: write and run notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core

popup.title: Gabor plots a drifting sensor
popup.body: At the counter with the two stools, Gabor plots a week of rooftop readings and spots a drifting sensor. The JupyterLab notebook runs its code on the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Sorrel drafts the supplier enquiry
popup.body: A sensor board has failed. Gabor messages Sorrel the part name, and Sorrel drafts a supplier note on the Core’s local model. Gabor reads it and sends it himself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: gabor
say.text: The supplier note is ready. Read it first, and send it when it looks right.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: A game starts from the sectional
popup.body: After school, Bence signs in with his own Valve account. Steam Headless runs Steam on the Core, and a browser on the TV shows it.
popup.note: Steam needs a Valve account. A Core may lack the graphics power a game wants.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: The school concert plays again
popup.body: Before lunch, Bence puts on the film Gabor made at Reka’s school concert. Jellyfin plays it from the Core to the TV, from the family’s own files.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Bence clears a full phone
popup.body: After the tournament weekend, Bence’s phone says it is full. Immich copies his photos to the Core and sorts them by date, so he can clear space on the phone.
popup.note: The first start takes a while.

beats.capability: manage and read books, comics and PDFs

popup.title: Reka opens the history chapter
popup.body: Reka’s teacher shared the term’s history reader as a PDF. She reads the next chapter in BookLore, and the file sits on the Core with the family’s books.
popup.note: BookLore fetches covers and details from the internet.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: Reka writes about a character
popup.body: On Saturday morning, Reka sits on the canopy bed and writes a character note for her class’s play. Obsidian keeps each note as a file on the Core.

beats.capability: chat with models running on your own Core, from any browser

popup.title: Reka checks her own working
popup.body: Reka solves a ratio problem herself, then asks a model on the Core to check her working in Open WebUI. The chat stays on the Core by default.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: Goulash moves a day later
popup.body: Training moves to Thursday, so Bence slides the goulash to Friday in Yuvomi, and the shopping list follows. One planner on the Core keeps the meal plan and the list.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Reka reads her grandmother’s card
popup.body: A card from Reka’s grandmother leans by the range, with a German line Reka cannot place. LibreTranslate translates it on the Core, and Reka writes her reply by hand.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals, notes, contacts and budget

popup.title: The month’s budget gets sorted
popup.body: On Sunday afternoon Eszter sorts the month’s spending into Yuvomi’s budget. Gabor reads the same budget, because the household shares one planner on the Core.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: Bence builds a welcome for cousins
popup.body: Cousins arrive on Saturday, so Bence builds a welcome scene in Home Assistant. One tap starts the fountain and the hall lantern together, and the Core runs it.
popup.note: Home Assistant needs no cloud account.

popup.title: A villa, four rooms, one Core
popup.body: One Companion Core on the Salon shelf serves four people, behind a fountain and cypress trees.

closing.body: Your documents, code, films and homework can run on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and choose your first apps.

notes: No beat uses an app without a QA screenshot (Code Server, Ollama, Calibre-Web and Mealie left out), so reviewed.json needs no kovacs entry. The household suite is LibreOffice, one suite per household.
The house has no desk, only the Core shelf. Gabor works at the Games Den trestle table, the counter with two stools and the fireplace; the text never says desk.
In the resolver the Salon, Games Den and TV Room are living rooms by area: room living nth 0 is the Salon, nth 2 the TV Room. Couch nth 0 and 1 are the Salon sofas, nth 2 the sectional.
bed nth 2 with room bedroom is the West Bedroom canopy bed. The garden role resolves to the forecourt fountain, so the garden beat stands at the front after the kitchen.
Both agents run Hermes: the chat note rides on ftue-hello, salon-draft and den-sorrel. The only Companion Memory mention is in salon-draft. In every agent beat the person reads and sends.
Steam Headless: Valve account named, no frame rate, no title, home network only. west-homework uses the replaces ChatGPT chip; the text names a model on the Core and never a cloud key.
Pi-hole covers only devices that use it for DNS, one household instance set up by Gabor. Home Assistant needs no cloud account of its own; the fountain pump and hall lantern sit on network devices.
west-reading carries the BookLore cloud-link note (covers and details come from outside). salon-dns carries the privacy topic.
